_comment: Fragment 88 — D-132: two open items reframed by ownership rather than by content, and one of them found never to have been the decision-maker's to answer at all. Merged 2026-08-25.

nodes.label: Two Open Gaps Reframed by Ownership, Not by Content
nodes.description: Before asking a decision-maker for more input, the remaining sub-questions of two open gaps were checked against what a just-issued ruling had already settled and against who actually held each remaining question, revealing that neither gap's substance had changed but the party who owed an answer had.
nodes.rationale: A gap's tracked status can go stale in its ownership even while its content stays accurate, and that staleness costs a decision-maker's attention the same way a stale ask does. Checking ownership before escalating is what kept a near-zero-input request from being framed as though it needed a ruling.

nodes.label: A Gap's Own Text Had Already Said It Was a Sequencing Dependency
nodes.description: A gap framed as waiting on a business decision had stated its actual blocker — a piece of infrastructure not yet built — in its own original text from the moment it was opened, and no pass before this one had read that sentence as dispositive.
nodes.rationale: The evidence that a question was never a decision was present at the point the question was first recorded, not discovered by new analysis. Naming it required re-reading an existing entry for what it already said rather than producing new information.
